# React Blender Panels

Blender-style panels for React. Give it a div to fill and it splits into panels you can resize by
dragging an edge, and split or join by dragging a corner.

One component, no stylesheet, no dependencies beyond React. About 4.3 KB gzipped.

## The model

A layout is a flat array of rectangles, each one a panel, together tiling the div exactly. The
fractions add up and nothing overlaps. No tree and no groups, so adjacency is just geometry.

```ts
interface Panel {
  id: string
  x: number // left edge, as a fraction of the div (0–1)
  y: number // top edge
  w: number // width
  h: number // height
}
```

Because they are fractions rather than pixels, the same array works at any size, and it serialises
as plain JSON.

## Getting started

You own the panels. Pass in an array and save the new one handed back after every gesture.

```tsx
import { Panels } from 'react-blender-panels'
import type { Panel } from 'react-blender-panels'

const [panels, setPanels] = useState<Panel[]>([
  { id: 'viewport',   x: 0,   y: 0,   w: 0.7, h: 1   },
  { id: 'outliner',   x: 0.7, y: 0,   w: 0.3, h: 0.4 },
  { id: 'properties', x: 0.7, y: 0.4, w: 0.3, h: 0.6 },
])

<div style={{ width: '100%', height: 500 }}>
  <Panels value={panels} onChange={setPanels}>
    {(panel) => <div>{panel.id}</div>}
  </Panels>
</div>
```

## Your content

Pass a function as the child. It runs once for each panel and returns what to render inside it.
`Panel` is the minimum shape the library needs. Add your own fields and they come back to you
typed, both in that function and from `onChange`.

```tsx
const CONTENT = {
  viewport: Viewport,
  outliner: Outliner,
  properties: Properties,
}

interface MyPanel extends Panel {
  kind: keyof typeof CONTENT
}

<Panels value={panels} onChange={setPanels}>
  {(panel) => {
    const Content = CONTENT[panel.kind]
    return <Content />
  }}
</Panels>
```

Your own fields ride along untouched, which is what makes this work. Split a panel and the new one
is a copy, so it renders the same content until you change it. A panel switcher is just setting
`kind` on one panel and saving the array, so the arrangement and what is in it save together.

Your component fills the panel on its own. Panels are grid containers w/ a `minmax(0, 1fr)` track,
so a single child stretches to the rectangle and may shrink below its own content. What happens to
content that no longer fits (scroll, clip, ellipsis) is yours to decide. The library never clips a
panel, so your dropdowns and tooltips can escape it.

## Props

`<Panels>`

- `value: Panel[]`. The panels.
- `onChange: (panels: Panel[]) => void`. The next panels after a gesture. Save it, render from it.
- `children: (panel: Panel) => ReactNode`. What to render inside each panel.
- `minSize?: number`. Pixels. No panel is dragged or split below this. Default 24.
- `className?: string`, `style?: CSSProperties`. Applied to the library's own div.

## Gestures

Three, and they all live on the panels themselves.

- **Resize**. Drag a shared edge. Every panel touching that line moves w/ it, live, so the panels
  follow the pointer.
- **Split**. Drag a corner inward. It divides where you release. Sideways gives you a seam down the
  middle, up or down gives you one across.
- **Join**. Drag a corner across into a neighbour. Your panel takes its space. Only legal where the
  two share a whole side, since anything else would leave a hole.

Split and join preview while you drag and commit when you let go. Escape cancels from anywhere.

## Styling

The panels are yours so their look is your CSS. The library ships no stylesheet. The geometry the
gestures depend on travels inline, and everything else is a custom property you can set on the
component or anywhere above it.

```tsx
const style = {
  '--rbp-gap': '6px',                        // between panels, never around them
  '--rbp-edge-size': '8px',                // grab reach either side of an edge handle
  '--rbp-corner-size': '12px',               // the corner handle's square

  '--rbp-edge-color': 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3)',  // the line a hovered edge handle shows
  '--rbp-corner-color': 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3)',    // a hovered corner handle, defaults to the edge colour
  '--rbp-preview-border': 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55)', // outline of what a release would do
  '--rbp-preview-fill': 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.04)',   // and its wash
  '--rbp-preview-radius': '4px',
  '--rbp-preview-fade': '240ms',             // how long a preview takes to appear

  '--rbp-cursor-corner': 'crosshair',        // over a corner handle
  '--rbp-cursor-resize-x': 'col-resize',     // over a vertical edge
  '--rbp-cursor-resize-y': 'row-resize',     // over a horizontal edge
  '--rbp-cursor-join-e': 'e-resize',         // about to swallow the neighbour east
  '--rbp-cursor-join-w': 'w-resize',
  '--rbp-cursor-join-n': 'n-resize',
  '--rbp-cursor-join-s': 's-resize',
  '--rbp-cursor-blocked': 'not-allowed',     // this gesture is illegal here
}

<Panels value={panels} onChange={setPanels} style={style}>
  {(panel) => <MyContent panel={panel} />}
</Panels>
```

Set `--rbp-edge-color` and `--rbp-corner-color` to `transparent` to keep the gestures working with
no visual feedback. Set `--rbp-edge-size` or `--rbp-corner-size` to `0px` to remove the hit areas
themselves.

The gap only ever appears *between* panels. Each panel gives up half a gap on every side that has a
neighbour and nothing on the sides that touch the container. For space around the outside, use
padding on your own div.

Every element the library renders has a stable class: `.rbp-panels`, `.rbp-panel`, `.rbp-edge-handle`,
`.rbp-line`, `.rbp-corner-handle`, `.rbp-preview`.
